answer: The echo multiplier is published, charged in gale, and lotus lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 1902 identities would post 557 proofs and burn roughly 59 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
